breakthroughs.insight: The waiters never poured for seat 1, yet a gold-rimmed flute was standing at Chief Bankole's place at 19:32. It wasn't there at 19:25. Someone else put it there.
The first dance was planned for 20:15. A call on the planners' radio channel moved it to 19:26 and blacked out every table for four minutes, just as Chief left his seat to spray the couple.
The woman at seat 1 in the dark wore wine aso-ebi with a planner's earpiece and gold wristband. Only one planner ordered a wine set: Ronke Bello.
Ronke says she was in the kitchen corridor with her cake team all through the blackout. Her own team could not find her anywhere from 19:27 to 19:31.
Dr Eze's car left at 18:52 and came back at 19:58. She was not in the hall when the glass appeared.
Ronke Bello was born Ronke Ajayi: the daughter who testified in the land case her father lost to Chief Bankole, months before he died.
Chief, Folake (in her gold gele) and Kayode were all on the dance floor during the blackout. The woman at seat 1 was someone else.

revealLines.text: …I knew who he was. Everybody in Abijo knows who he is. That case was my father's, not mine. I took this job because I needed the work.

All right, we argued. About my betting. He found out I owed eighteen million. He shouted, then at half six he paid it all and told me if I ever bet again, I'm on my own. Why would I kill the one man who had just saved me?
Fine. I went out to the car park to call my bank manager. There was a transfer that had to be reversed before Monday. I was outside maybe fifteen minutes.
Okay, I made the call. The couple were ready and we were behind schedule. That is not a crime.

debrief.text: Pa Joseph Ajayi loses his family land at Abijo to Bankole Homes in Suit LD/1187/2019. His daughter Ronke testifies for him. He dies in March 2022.
Now Ronke Bello, she wins the Bankole wedding with a "miracle" price, then orders a wine aso-ebi set "for family photos".
She adds a line to the MC's run sheet: "Daddy, today you must drink with us!", and a note that the first dance may move.
She signs out bottle #24 "for the couple's room". In Room B she pours one of her two Lumière flutes and stirs in her late father's digoxin.
On the planners' channel she tells the DJ to start the first dance now. Cue 14 blacks out every table; Chief goes down to spray the couple.
In the dark she sets the flute at seat 1. A guest's flash catches her back: wine gele, earpiece wire, gold wristband.
At 19:32 the waiters skip seat 1, as instructed. The MC reads her line and sees the glass is "already there". Chief drinks, "just this once".
Chief collapses. Ronke tries twice to have the high-table glasses cleared; the head waiter and Dr Eze refuse.
Police seal Room B with the empty pill bottle, labelled for J. Ajayi, and the twin of the flute still inside.
